title: GitHub Projects
definition: A customizable project management tool integrated directly into GitHub. It allows you to create Kanban boards, spreadsheets, and roadmaps to organize Issues and Pull Requests.
simpleExplanation: Trello or Jira, but built directly inside GitHub. You create a board with columns like 'To Do', 'In Progress', and 'Done'. You can drag and drop your GitHub Issues between the columns as you work on them.
realWorldExample: A project manager creates a Kanban board. During the morning standup meeting, they drag the 'Fix database bug' issue from the 'To Do' column into the 'In Progress' column, and assign it to a developer.

intermediate: Can a GitHub Project board automatically move an issue to 'Done' when a Pull Request is merged?

answers.question: What is Kanban?
answers.answer: A visual system for managing work as it moves through a process. It uses cards (Issues) and columns (To Do, Doing, Done) to visualize the workflow.

answers.question: Automate moving to Done?
answers.answer: Yes! GitHub Projects have built-in automation workflows. You can tell it: 'When an issue is closed, automatically drag its card into the Done column'.

codeExample:
/*
  A typical GitHub Project Kanban Board Layout:
  
  [ Backlog ]   |   [ To Do (Sprint) ]   |   [ In Progress ]   |   [ Review ]   |   [ Done ]
  ------------  |   ------------------   |   ---------------   |   ----------   |   --------
  Issue #99     |   Issue #45            |   Issue #42         |   PR #44       |   Issue #12
  Issue #100    |   Issue #48            |                     |                |   Issue #14
*/
